text:
maria_s: FYI CVE flagged by Snyk for grpc + oauth2 usage in our runtime. advisory link: https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-GOLANG-GRPC-2026 . Looks like token parsing vulnerability in oauth/jwt libs we vendor. Can we triage impact + rollout plan?

samir: thanks. quick read — CVE impacts token parsing on older oauth libs; requires crafted token to trigger. CVSS 7.2 in advisory. Our public hosted API could be exposed but attack complexity non-trivial. Need concrete dependency list first.

alexw: I pulled `go.sum` and grep'd for `google.golang.org/grpc` and `github.com/coreos/go-oidc` — we have grpc@v1.52.0 and go-oidc pinned indirectly via `authz` service at v0.0.0-202305. Repro steps in my fork: `grep -R "go-oidc" -n` on repo.

jin_chen: can you paste the exact `go get` upgrade commands? I can open a hotfix PR and run CI.

alexw: sure — `go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.54.0` and `go get github.com/coreos/go-oidc@v0.10.0` (these are the patched releases referenced in advisory). also add a `replace` fallback in go.mod for services still resolving older transitive versions.

samir: +1 for patching. Two angles: 1) fast hotpatch to hosted runtime (canary -> full) 2) backport to maintained release branches (v1.12, v1.11) for Dedicated/private customers. Recommend canary on a small percentage of requests for 24h.

security-bot: automated scan results: 5 occurrences of vulnerable transitive dependency across monorepo. Affected services: runtime-serving, api-proxy, authz. Suggested PR template: include CVE id, upgrade commands, CI smoke, and audit log review.

maria_s: Ops implications? Do we need to rotate keys or disable any endpoints? Any KMS or audit logs touched?

jin_chen: no KMS rotation required — vuln is parsing-related, not key compromise. But let's increase audit logging for identity flows for 48h post-rollout. Add temporary elevated logging for token validation endpoints (keep logs for 14 days in case of investigation). That requires infra change in env config.

alexw: opened PR #4321 with `go get` upgrades + `go mod tidy` + a `replace` in `authz/go.mod` to pin transitive patch. CI ran unit + integration tests. smoke shows no perf delta. PR description has impact notes and links to advisory.

samir: I'll schedule canary tomorrow at 03:00 UTC: route 2% traffic via canary pool in us-west-2 (dedicated canary nodes). If no errors/tagged incidents in 24h we roll to 100% with a 1h step-up. Also backport plan: open backport PRs against release/v1.12 and release/v1.11 after canary passes.

maria_s: sounds good. for private deployments we should notify account owners and provide a small patch script: `go mod edit -replace=github.com/coreos/go-oidc=github.com/coreos/go-oidc@v0.10.0` and instructions to run `go mod tidy && vendor`. Add notes about offline air-gapped installs (they need the vendor tarball).

ops-bot: scheduled canary job created: job id canary-2026-04-11-0300. Watchlink: https://internal.ops/canaries/canary-2026-04-11-0300

samir: one more ask — add a quick fuzz test for token parsing in our authz suite, to prevent regressions. If someone can add it in the backport PR that would be ideal.

jin_chen: I'll add a small fuzz harness and attach to CI as a nightly job.

maria_s: closing loop — assigns: samir (canary ops), alexw (PR + backports), jin_chen (fuzz tests + audit logging config), maria_s (customer comms for private). Thanks team :thumbsup:

security-bot: note: please add CVE and mitigation notes to changelog and run stack-scanner after final rollout.

alexw: will do, PR description updated with changelog entry and mitigation steps.

maria_s: marking this thread resolved once canary completes. keep any post-mortem if we see anomalies.
